plants.description: Tomato is a common fruit crop that is vulnerable to foliar diseases when humidity, leaf wetness, and poor airflow are high.

diseases.description: Healthy tomato foliage is usually uniform green and without widespread spotting, lesions, or yellowing.
prevention: Remove weak or diseased material promptly
plant-care advice: Water at the base of the plant when possible
Provide enough light and avoid overwatering
Monitor leaves every few days for early changes
treatment guidance: No disease treatment is required when the plant is healthy. Continue regular care and monitoring.
notes: Healthy plants should continue to be observed for stress, nutrient issues, or emerging disease.

diseases.description: Early blight is a common tomato foliar disease caused by fungal organisms that thrive in warm, humid conditions.
symptoms: Brown to dark leaf spots with concentric rings
common contributing conditions: Leaf wetness from dew or overhead irrigation
prevention: Water at soil level instead of on foliage
Remove infected lower leaves and debris
plant-care advice: Keep the canopy open and avoid repeated wetness on leaves
Maintain balanced nutrition to support recovery
Check lower leaves regularly for early lesions
treatment guidance: Use a locally approved product for this crop and disease according to the product label and agricultural guidance.
Follow regional disease-management recommendations for tomato crops.
notes: Early detection and sanitation can reduce spread.
If symptoms are severe or spreading quickly, consult a local agricultural advisor.

diseases.description: Late blight can spread quickly in cool and wet weather, causing rapid foliar damage and plant stress.
symptoms: Rapid spread under cool, wet conditions
common contributing conditions: High humidity and persistent leaf wetness
Nearby infected plants or volunteer hosts
prevention: Sanitize tools and remove infected tissue
plant-care advice: Monitor the crop closely after rainy periods
Inspect stems and leaves for new lesions
treatment guidance: Use a locally approved product for this crop and disease according to the product label and agricultural guidance.
Follow a local integrated disease-management plan for late blight.
notes: Late blight can become severe quickly under damp conditions.

diseases.description: Bacterial spot can cause water-soaked lesions and is often linked to splashing water and warm, wet conditions.
symptoms: Small dark lesions with yellow halos
Possible fruit lesions in severe cases
prevention: Reduce leaf wetness and improve airflow
plant-care advice: Maintain proper spacing and avoid stress
Scout often after periods of rain
treatment guidance: Use a locally approved product for this crop and disease according to the product label and agricultural guidance.
Apply a disease-management plan suited to local tomato production conditions.
notes: Bacterial diseases often require sanitation and the reduction of leaf wetness.

plants.description: Potato leaves can show disease patterns that often intensify under cool, wet, or crowded plant conditions.

diseases.description: Healthy potato foliage is typically green and evenly balanced without major spots or wilting.
prevention: Scout useful areas before symptoms spread
plant-care advice: Maintain even watering and crop nutrition
Remove weeds and monitor for stress
Keep the canopy open to reduce humidity
treatment guidance: No disease treatment is needed when the crop appears healthy. Continue standard agricultural care.
notes: Healthy crops should still be checked periodically for early disease outbreaks.

diseases.description: Early blight often appears as dark spots with concentric patterning on older potato leaves.
symptoms: Higher disease pressure on older leaves
common contributing conditions: Stress from nutrient imbalance or poor air movement
prevention: Remove infected material from the field
plant-care advice: Support plant vigor with balanced nutrition
Keep records of weather and symptom progression
treatment guidance: Use a locally approved product for this crop and disease according to the product label and agricultural guidance.
Base management decisions on local potato disease recommendations.
notes: The disease may progress steadily if left unchecked in warm wet weather.

diseases.description: Late blight is a serious potato disease that spreads rapidly under cool and wet conditions.
symptoms: Rapid crop decline under moist weather
common contributing conditions: Contaminated crop residue or nearby infected plants
prevention: Use rotation and sanitation where practical
plant-care advice: Inspect the upper and lower canopy
treatment guidance: Use a locally approved product for this crop and disease according to the product label and agricultural guidance.
Follow a local emergency disease-management program when conditions are favorable for spread.
notes: Rapid intervention is often needed in severe disease pressure.

plants.description: Pepper plants can suffer foliar disease when warmth, humidity, and poor airflow combine in the crop canopy.

diseases.description: Healthy pepper leaves are usually green and firm without widespread spots or wilting.
plant-care advice: Use consistent watering and avoid overfeeding
Look for early symptoms after high humidity
treatment guidance: No disease treatment is needed when the plant appears healthy. Continue standard care and monitoring.
notes: Healthy pepper plants benefit from regular observation and good airflow.

diseases.description: Bacterial spot in peppers often appears as small dark lesions with yellow margins and can spread with splashing water.
symptoms: Possible fruit spots in severe cases
plant-care advice: Avoid practices that splash water from leaf to leaf
treatment guidance: Use a locally approved product for this crop and disease according to the product label and agricultural guidance.
Follow local pepper disease management advice for the region.
notes: Managing humidity and leaf wetness is important for limiting spread.

diseases.description: Leaf mold is a foliar disease often associated with warm, humid greenhouse or protected cropping environments.
symptoms: Mold growth on the undersides of leaves
Yellowing and leaf collapse in severe cases
prevention: Water at the base and avoid wet foliage
plant-care advice: Avoid letting the canopy stay wet overnight
Use routine sanitation in protected cropping spaces
treatment guidance: Use a locally approved product for this crop and disease according to the product label and agricultural guidance.
Follow local protected-crop recommendations for fungal control and ventilation.
notes: Leaf mold is often linked to poor ventilation and persistently humid conditions.

plants.description: Chilli plants are often affected by foliar disease when humidity and wet leaves persist over time.

diseases.description: Healthy chilli plants usually have firm, uniformly green leaves and steady growth without lesions.
prevention: Keep leaf surfaces dry when practical
plant-care advice: Monitor for stress and early disease symptoms
treatment guidance: No disease treatment is required when the plant is healthy. Continue routine care and monitoring.
notes: Routine monitoring is useful for identifying emerging disease before it spreads.

diseases.description: Leaf mold in chilli plants often develops when the canopy stays humid for long periods and airflow is limited.
plant-care advice: Inspect undersides of leaves for symptoms
Use a watering strategy that keeps foliage dry
Remove severely affected leaves if needed
treatment guidance: Use a locally approved product for this crop and disease according to the product label and agricultural guidance.
Follow local crop-protection recommendations for chilli production.
notes: Managing humidity is critical in preventing mold spread in chilli plants.

diseases.description: Septoria leaf spot is a foliar problem that often begins as small circular lesions and spreads under moist conditions.
symptoms: Small circular spots with darker centers
Yellowing and leaf drop in severe cases
Progressive symptom spread on older foliage
prevention: Improve airflow and reduce overhead irrigation
Sanitize and remove heavily affected leaves
Monitor after rainfall or dew periods
plant-care advice: Check lower leaves early and often
Keep the crop healthy to reduce stress
treatment guidance: Use a locally approved product for this crop and disease according to the product label and agricultural guidance.
Follow local disease-control recommendations suited to chilli production.
notes: Regular scouting reduces the chance that leaf spot spreads unnoticed.

plants.description: Paddy is a major cereal crop grown in wet or flooded conditions, and it is highly sensitive to water stress, nutrient imbalance, and foliar disease outbreaks.

diseases.description: Healthy paddy plants have uniform green leaves and steady tillering with no significant lesion spread.
symptoms: No major leaf spotting or wilting
prevention: Practice field hygiene and crop rotation
plant-care advice: Inspect leaves regularly for stress or disease
treatment guidance: No disease treatment is required when the crop is healthy. Continue standard crop management and monitoring.
notes: Healthy paddy fields benefit from stable water management and regular inspection.

diseases.description: Rice blast is a serious fungal disease that damages leaves and panicles especially in humid conditions with uneven moisture.
symptoms: Leaf drying and tip burn in severe cases
prevention: Keep field conditions balanced and well managed
plant-care advice: Scout early and often during humid periods
Keep the field well drained and healthy
Remove infected residues from the field when possible
treatment guidance: Use a locally approved product for this crop and disease according to the product label and agricultural guidance.
Follow local rice disease management recommendations.
notes: Blast can spread rapidly under favorable humidity and poor crop management.

diseases.description: Brown spot causes dark circular lesions on leaves and often becomes severe when the crop is under nutrient stress.
symptoms: Brown circular leaf spots with yellow halos
prevention: Improve field health and moisture control
plant-care advice: Check the field after periods of stress
Apply nutrients according to soil recommendations
Monitor leaf symptoms by field section
treatment guidance: Use a locally approved product for this crop and disease according to the product label and agricultural guidance.
Follow the recommended agronomic practices for field rice production.
notes: Strong crop nutrition and field management can reduce disease severity.

plants.description: Brinjal is a warm-season vegetable crop whose leaves and fruits can be impacted by foliar disease and wilt under humid or stressed conditions.

diseases.description: Healthy brinjal plants have strong leaves, balanced growth, and no major spots or wilting symptoms.
plant-care advice: Check leaves often for early symptoms
Keep the crop free from stress and debris
treatment guidance: No disease treatment is needed when the crop appears healthy. Continue regular care and monitoring.
notes: Well-managed brinjal plants remain vigorous and productive when monitored consistently.

diseases.description: Brinjal wilt often causes drooping, yellowing, and sudden decline in affected plants, especially under stress or soil-borne pressure.
prevention: Use clean seedling material and sanitation
plant-care advice: Inspect roots and stems when wilting appears
Remove affected plants to reduce spread
treatment guidance: Use a locally approved product for this crop and disease according to the product label and agricultural guidance.
Follow local brinjal crop protection recommendations.
notes: Wilt can rapidly reduce plant productivity if the soil and irrigation conditions are poor.

diseases.description: Fruit rot in brinjal is often linked to wet fruit surfaces, high humidity, and poor canopy ventilation.
common contributing conditions: Fruit contact with wet soil or leaves
plant-care advice: Mulch carefully and keep the soil clean
treatment guidance: Use a locally approved product for this crop and disease according to the product label and agricultural guidance.
Follow local fruit-protection recommendations for brinjal.
notes: Harvesting and sanitation reduce the spread of fruit rot in brinjal.

plants.description: Coriander is a leafy herb crop that is sensitive to moisture, humidity, and nutrient imbalance, especially in warm growing seasons.

diseases.description: Healthy coriander plants have fresh green leaves with steady, vigorous growth and no visible disease lesions.
prevention: Avoid leaf wetness for long periods
plant-care advice: Check leaves for symptoms after cool wet periods
treatment guidance: No disease treatment is needed when the crop is healthy. Continue regular crop management.
notes: Healthy coriander grows best with consistent moisture and careful field inspection.

diseases.description: Leaf spot in coriander often appears as brown circular lesions and spreads more rapidly under warm, wet conditions.
symptoms: Brown to dark spots on leaves
common contributing conditions: Poor spacing and dense crop canopy
prevention: Reduce leaf wetness and improve airflow
plant-care advice: Keep the crop canopy open and healthy
treatment guidance: Use a locally approved product for this crop and disease according to the product label and agricultural guidance.
notes: Coriander leaf spot is more manageable when moisture and canopy density are controlled.

diseases.description: Powdery mildew in coriander develops on leaf surfaces under dry but humid conditions and can reduce plant vigor.
plant-care advice: Keep the crop healthy and unstressed
Remove heavily affected foliage when needed
treatment guidance: Use a locally approved product for this crop and disease according to the product label and agricultural guidance.
notes: Powdery mildew is often easier to manage when the canopy is kept open and airy.

plants.description: Onion is a high-value vegetable crop that can develop foliar disease when humidity, leaf wetness, and poor airflow remain high.

diseases.description: Healthy onion plants have strong green leaves and a steady canopy without large lesions or yellowing.
prevention: Keep the crop weed-free and well spaced
plant-care advice: Monitor leaves for stress and response to irrigation
Check for disease after long wet periods
treatment guidance: No disease treatment is needed when the crop is healthy. Continue standard agronomic care.
notes: Healthy onion fields benefit from consistent water and field inspection.

diseases.description: Purple blotch is a common onion foliar disease that spreads rapidly under warm and humid weather conditions.
common contributing conditions: Leaf wetness and poor wind movement
prevention: Remove diseased plant material when practical
plant-care advice: Scout the crop during high humidity periods
Keep irrigation directed at the soil rather than leaves
treatment guidance: Use a locally approved product for this crop and disease according to the product label and agricultural guidance.
notes: Purple blotch becomes more serious when foliage remains wet for long periods.

plants.description: Okra is a warm-season vegetable crop that responds strongly to heat, moisture, and disease pressure in the canopy.

diseases.description: Healthy okra plants have firm green leaves and steady fruit development without widespread lesions.
plant-care advice: Monitor for leaf stress during hot periods
treatment guidance: No disease treatment is needed when the crop is healthy. Continue routine care and monitoring.
notes: Healthy okra crops are easier to manage when stress factors are kept low.

diseases.description: Yellow vein mosaic is a viral disease that can reduce growth and distort leaves, especially where the vector population is high.
plant-care advice: Inspect leaves for mosaic symptoms often
Monitor vector activity in the field
treatment guidance: Use a locally approved product for this crop and disease according to the product label and agricultural guidance.
Follow local recommendations for vector control and field hygiene.
notes: The disease is often spread by sucking insects, so vector management is important.

plants.description: Wheat is a cereal crop that is highly sensitive to nutrient imbalance, water stress, and foliar disease during key growth stages.

diseases.description: Healthy wheat has deep green leaves, strong tillering, and good grain filling without widespread lesion spread.
symptoms: No major yellowing or leaf lesions
plant-care advice: Check crop vigor early in the season
Scout for stress after weather swings
treatment guidance: No disease treatment is needed when the crop is healthy. Continue standard agronomic care.
notes: Healthy wheat depends on balanced nutrition and regular field scouting.

diseases.description: Leaf rust is a common wheat disease that reduces photosynthesis and grain quality under favorable humid conditions.
symptoms: Orange or rust-colored pustules on leaves
Reduced grain filling in severe cases
plant-care advice: Scout fields frequently during humid periods
Maintain good crop health and nutrient balance
treatment guidance: Use a locally approved product for this crop and disease according to the product label and agricultural guidance.
notes: Rust severity often increases quickly when weather stays humid and the crop is stressed.

plants.description: Maize is a major cereal crop whose health depends on balanced nutrition, root vigor, and disease monitoring during the growing season.

diseases.description: Healthy maize plants have vigorous green leaves and strong upright growth with no widespread lesion development.
symptoms: No major yellowing or lesion spread
plant-care advice: Watch the crop after rainfall and heat stress
Support root health with proper nutrition
Keep the field clean and well managed
treatment guidance: No disease treatment is needed when the crop is healthy. Continue standard field management.
notes: Maize remains productive when nutrient and moisture management are consistent.

diseases.description: Leaf blight in maize can reduce photosynthesis and plant vigor when conditions stay humid and the canopy remains dense.
prevention: Use good sanitation and resistant varieties
plant-care advice: Scout the field frequently during humid weather
Remove heavy disease pressure where feasible
treatment guidance: Use a locally approved product for this crop and disease according to the product label and agricultural guidance.
notes: Disease pressure often increases when the field remains humid and canopy density is high.

plants.description: Banana is a high-yield fruit crop where moisture balance, nutrient availability, and leaf health are critical to productivity.

diseases.description: Healthy banana plants have green broad leaves and vigorous growth without extensive spotting or collapse.
plant-care advice: Monitor leaves for stress and wilting
Protect root health and moisture balance
Keep the plantation clean and stable
treatment guidance: No disease treatment is required when the crop is healthy. Continue regular management.
notes: Healthy banana fields require regular maintenance and monitoring for early stress.

diseases.description: Sigatoka is a leaf spot disease that affects banana foliage and can reduce photosynthesis and yield if not managed.
symptoms: Light streaks or spots on leaves
treatment guidance: Use a locally approved product for this crop and disease according to the product label and agricultural guidance.
notes: Early sanitation and field monitoring can reduce the spread of Sigatoka.

plants.description: Groundnut is a legume crop whose pod and leaf health depend strongly on soil condition, moisture balance, and disease avoidance.

diseases.description: Healthy groundnut plants have strong green leaves and balanced growth without major lesion spread.
plant-care advice: Maintain soil health and root development
Scout for stress in leaves and pods
treatment guidance: No disease treatment is needed when the crop is healthy. Continue regular agronomic care.
notes: Healthy groundnut can produce well when soil and moisture conditions are stable.

diseases.description: Groundnut leaf spot is often associated with wet periods and poor canopy conditions that favor foliar disease spread.
plant-care advice: Scouting and sanitation help reduce spread
Keep the field well managed during rainy weather
Remove severely infected foliage when practical
treatment guidance: Use a locally approved product for this crop and disease according to the product label and agricultural guidance.
notes: Groundnut diseases are often easier to manage when the canopy stays healthy and dry.

plants.description: Sugarcane is a tall field crop grown for sucrose production and is sensitive to moisture stress, nutrient imbalance, and foliar disease.

diseases.description: Healthy sugarcane has vigorous green stalks and strong leaf growth with no widespread lesions.
prevention: Keep the field healthy and clean
treatment guidance: No disease treatment is required when the crop is healthy. Continue regular agronomic care.
notes: Healthy sugarcane is best maintained with regular field checks.

diseases.description: Red rot is a destructive sugarcane disease that reduces cane quality and can lead to severe yield loss.
treatment guidance: Use a locally approved product for this crop and disease according to the product label and agricultural guidance.
notes: Red rot can seriously reduce cane quality and field productivity.

plants.description: Cotton is a major fiber crop where leaf health, moisture balance, and pest pressure strongly influence field performance.

diseases.description: Healthy cotton plants show strong leaf growth, steady plant structure, and normal fruiting.
treatment guidance: No disease treatment is needed when the crop is healthy. Continue regular field management.
notes: Healthy cotton fields benefit from balanced crop monitoring.

diseases.description: Leaf curl in cotton usually reduces vigor and can cause malformed leaves and lower productivity.
treatment guidance: Use a locally approved product for this crop and disease according to the product label and agricultural guidance.
notes: Vector management and field hygiene are important in reducing spread.

plants.description: Cucumber is a fast-growing vegetable crop that is highly sensitive to foliar disease and wet canopy conditions.

diseases.description: Healthy cucumber plants have bright green leaves and steady vine development without widespread lesions.
treatment guidance: No disease treatment is needed when the crop is healthy. Continue regular care.
notes: Healthy cucumbers benefit from moderate, consistent crop care.

diseases.description: Powdery mildew is a common cucumber disease that can reduce vigor and fruit quality under warm humid conditions.
treatment guidance: Use a locally approved product for this crop and disease according to the product label and agricultural guidance.

plants.description: Cabbage is a leafy vegetable crop where disease risk often rises with dense foliage, poor airflow, and prolonged leaf wetness.

diseases.description: Healthy cabbage leaves are firm, dense, and uniformly green with no major lesion development.
treatment guidance: No disease treatment is needed when the crop is healthy. Continue standard care.
notes: Healthy cabbage responds well to regular field inspection.

diseases.description: Black rot is a serious cabbage disease that causes leaf yellowing, necrosis, and poor market quality.
prevention: Use clean seed and healthy transplants
plant-care advice: Keep the crop clean and healthy
treatment guidance: Use a locally approved product for this crop and disease according to the product label and agricultural guidance.
notes: Black rot can spread quickly when wet conditions persist.

plants.description: Cauliflower is a cool-season crop that is highly sensitive to temperature stress, moisture imbalance, and foliar disease.

diseases.description: Healthy cauliflower heads are compact and leaves are uniformly green with strong growth.
treatment guidance: No disease treatment is needed when the crop is healthy. Continue regular care.
notes: Healthy cauliflower is benefited by regular moisture and nutrient checks.

diseases.description: Downy mildew is a foliar disease of cauliflower that can spread rapidly under cool, humid conditions.
treatment guidance: Use a locally approved product for this crop and disease according to the product label and agricultural guidance.
notes: Managing humidity and leaf wetness is key to disease reduction.

plants.description: Mango is an orchard crop where tree health, canopy conditions, and disease control strongly influence fruit quality and yield.

diseases.description: Healthy mango trees have dense green foliage, strong growth, and normal fruit development.
treatment guidance: No disease treatment is needed when the tree is healthy. Continue standard orchard care.
notes: Healthy mango trees require regular monitoring and orchard hygiene.

diseases.description: Anthracnose is a common mango disease that affects leaves, flowers, and fruit under wet conditions.
symptoms: Dark lesions on leaves and fruit
treatment guidance: Use a locally approved product for this crop and disease according to the product label and agricultural guidance.
notes: Anthracnose can spread rapidly during wet and humid periods.

plants.description: Grapevine is a fruit crop where canopy management, humidity control, and disease scouting are important for vine health.

diseases.description: Healthy grapevines have firm leaves and balanced growth with no major fungal or nutrient stress symptoms.
treatment guidance: No disease treatment is needed when the vine is healthy. Continue regular orchard care.
notes: Healthy grapevines benefit from regular canopy and moisture checks.

diseases.description: Powdery mildew in grapevine is a surface fungal issue that reduces leaf vigor and fruit quality under warm humid conditions.
plant-care advice: Act early when symptoms are seen
treatment guidance: Use a locally approved product for this crop and disease according to the product label and agricultural guidance.
notes: Good canopy management helps prevent rapid mildew spread.

plants.description: Soybean is a legume crop that depends on good root health, nutrient balance, and disease prevention during wet or warm conditions.

diseases.description: Healthy soybean plants have green leaves, strong stems, and consistent pod development.
plant-care advice: Inspect the crop throughout growth stages
treatment guidance: No disease treatment is needed when the crop is healthy. Continue standard management.
notes: Healthy soybean remains productive with consistent field management.

diseases.description: Soybean rust is a major foliar disease that reduces leaf area and can lower yield under conducive weather.
treatment guidance: Use a locally approved product for this crop and disease according to the product label and agricultural guidance.
notes: Rust can become severe in humid and dense crop conditions.

plants.description: Sunflower is a broad-acre oil crop where strong stem health, canopy structure, and foliar disease monitoring matter a lot.

diseases.description: Healthy sunflower plants show strong stems, bright green leaves, and normal head development.
plant-care advice: Inspect the crop at growth stages
treatment guidance: No disease treatment is needed when the crop is healthy. Continue standard field management.
notes: Healthy sunflower benefits from regular agronomic checks.

diseases.description: Leaf spot in sunflower can cause reduced photosynthesis and yield loss if it spreads through the canopy.
treatment guidance: Use a locally approved product for this crop and disease according to the product label and agricultural guidance.
notes: Leaf spot pressure is often greater in humid and dense stands.

plants.description: Coconut is a perennial plantation crop where tree vigor, canopy health, and moisture regularity strongly affect productivity.

diseases.description: Healthy coconut palms have strong fronds, steady growth, and normal nut development without major lesion spread.
treatment guidance: No disease treatment is needed when the palm is healthy. Continue regular plantation management.
notes: Healthy coconut palms benefit from regular field inspection and cleanliness.

diseases.description: Bud rot is a serious coconut disease that can quickly damage the growing point and lead to severe tree decline.
plant-care advice: Reduce moisture around the stem base
Remove severely affected palms when needed
treatment guidance: Use a locally approved product for this crop and disease according to the product label and agricultural guidance.
notes: Bud rot can cause major decline if moisture is not managed in the crown area.
